title: Investigate transient 5xx pattern during large tenant batch uploads + routing fallback behavior
creator: Marissa Gomez
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise tenants reported short-lived waves of 5xx responses and elevated timeouts while performing large batch uploads (multi-GB corpora) to the Hosted API. This incident appears correlated with: (1) high fanout from API proxy to model workers for large parallel requests, (2) routing fallback logic which triggers model-variant switchovers when a node is slow, and (3) ephemeral connection exhaustion on the proxy pool. Customers observed retry storms from their SDKs and saw degraded throughput for ~10-15 minutes before automatic graceful degradation kicked in.

Goals: identify the root cause(s), implement a short-term mitigation to stop customer-facing 5xx bursts, and implement a medium-term fix to routing and connection pool coordination so the platform can maintain stable latency and avoid retry amplification during tenant bursts.

What we know so far (Investigation notes):
- Incidents tracked in SRE dashboard for tenant: corp-ascend and corp-lumen at 2025-03-09T21:10-21:35 UTC.
- Pattern: sudden spike in request concurrency for a small subset of endpoints (bulk-index, embed-batch). Upstream proxy issued many concurrent connections to model pools.
- Proxy metrics show transient connection pool saturation (connection_wait_count spiked) and aggressive queued requests.
- Model worker traces show an increase in long tail kernel exec latency when sequence length variance > 1.2x, causing slow replies and triggering routing fallback which routes to alternate model variants.
- Routing fallback increases fanout because the proxy opens additional requests to alternate variants instead of failing fast. This amplified load on the model tier.
- SDK clients observed intermittent 502/504 and applied exponential backoff retries; due to lack of request-level idempotency keys for some batch endpoints, retries were non-idempotent and could cause duplicate processing downstream.
- KV cache hit ratio reduced during the burst due to mismatched cache keys for chunked uploads, causing more tokens to be recomputed.

Reproduction steps attempted:
1) Synthetic load simulating multi-part batch uploads from 120 concurrent connections using load generator 'rload' (script: https://go/infra/rload-scripts/batch-burst).
2) Observed same proxy connection_wait_count spike and 502s when we intentionally introduce 20% sequence-length variance in the payload.
3) Disable routing fallback in test environment -> errors drop but latency for some requests increases beyond SLO.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- Combination of: (A) proxy connection pool exhaustion + long-tail model kernel latency; (B) routing fallback strategy that opens additional fanout rather than backing off; and (C) insufficient idempotency semantics for bulk endpoints leading to retry amplification.

Short-term mitigations (to implement in next 24-72h):
- Patch proxy to enforce a hard-fail threshold when connection_wait_time > X ms (prevent indefinite fanout); deploy as canary to 10% of traffic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/1187
- Add quick rate limit and backpressure header for bulk endpoints (X-Redwood-Backpressure) so SDKs can slow client retry pacing. Draft SDK change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/764
- Server-side: add temporary per-tenant concurrency caps for bulk-index endpoints to reduce blast radius. Config change in control plane: https://go/configs/tenant-concurrency

Medium-term fixes (3-8 weeks):
- Rework routing fallback logic: instead of immediate additional fanout, implement circuit-breaker with exponential cooldown and a fast-fail option for high-cost endpoints. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Routing+Fallback+Revamp
- Improve connection pool telemetry and add adaptive pool sizing: increase min idle during detected tenant bursts and add shed-to-degraded-route policy.
- Add idempotency-key support for all bulk endpoints with deterministic dedupe semantics and metrics.
- KV cache key normalization for chunked uploads to maintain hit ratio across chunk boundaries.

Testing plan:
- Canary deploy proxy change to region us-west-2 with 5 tenants (non-production) and run rload script for 6 hours; compare 5xx rate and connection_wait_count.
- Unit/integration tests for idempotency dedupe logic with randomized chunk ordering.
- Load test routing fallback revamp in sandbox environment with scaled model worker pool and sequence length variance injection.

Acceptance criteria (must be strings in AC list):
- "5xx rate for bulk endpoints reduced to <= 0.05% during simulated tenant bursts in canary"
- "Proxy no longer opens multiple fallback fanout requests when connection_wait_time threshold exceeded"
- "Per-tenant bulk endpoint retries produce no duplicate side-effects when idempotency key supplied"
- "KV cache hit ratio returns to baseline (>80%) for chunked uploads in load tests"

Rollout and rollback plan:
- Deploy proxy patch to canary (10% traffic) -> monitor for 1 hour -> if error rate increases by >10% from baseline, rollback immediately.
- After canary validation (72h), promote to 50% and then full.
- Routing fallback revamp will be feature-flagged per region for phased rollout.

Customer comms:
- Draft external incident update prepared: https://go/comms/incidents/2025-03-09-bulk-upload-5xx-draft
- Proposed public note: apologize, summarize mitigations, offer weekly status until medium-term fixes complete, and offer credits for affected tenants (coordinating with CS).
